Description: The great glazed-brick gate of Nebuchadnezzar's Babylon, its blue walls decorated with bulls and serpent-dragons, excavated by Robert Koldewey and reconstructed in Berlin. It was one of eight gates in the inner city wall, opening onto the Processional Way.
BiblicalSignificance: This is the Babylon of Daniel's day made visible: the city Nebuchadnezzar boasted he had built by his mighty power. Walking through its gate in reconstruction, a reader can picture the splendour that made exile feel permanent — and the God who humbled its king.
Interpretations: Scholars agree the gate is Nebuchadnezzar's work of about 575 BC; the reconstruction in Berlin reassembles excavated bricks, with some modern brick completing the structure.
